title: Services, singletons and the scope an instance really has

videos.script:
Tick a session done on the course page, and the week's total does not move. Both numbers are right about their own copy of the data. That is the defect this lesson removes.

{{copies}} You watch it happen first: two requests for the same file, and two screens that disagree.

{{service}} Then a service. It is a class with no template, made once by the root injector. The planner store holds the one copy, and the only way to change it.

{{using}} Both screens ask for the store. One request now, and the week agrees with the course page.

{{readonly}} The store hands out signals that can only be read, and methods that change things. Try to write to it from outside, and the build stops you.

{{belongs}} You decide what moves into the store and what stays behind. A fact about the planner moves. A choice about one screen stays.

{{scope}} And you break it again, with one line. A singleton is only as single as where it is provided.
